continuous.

A continuous family of functions `α → β → γ` tends uniformly to its value at `x`
if `α` is weakly locally compact and `β` is compact.

Heine-Cantor: a continuous function on a compact uniform space is uniformly
continuous.

An equicontinuous family of functions defined on a compact uniform space is automatically
uniformly equicontinuous.

In a product space `α × β`, assume that a function `f` is continuous on `s × k` where `k` is
compact. Then, along the fiber above any `q ∈ s`, `f` is transversely uniformly continuous, i.e.,
if `p ∈ s` is close enough to `q`, then `f p x` is uniformly close to `f q x` for all `x ∈ k`.

If `s` is compact and `f` is continuous at all points of `s`, then `f` is
"uniformly continuous at the set `s`", i.e. `f x` is close to `f y` whenever `x ∈ s` and `y` is
close to `x` (even if `y` is not itself in `s`, so this is a stronger assertion than
`UniformContinuousOn s`).

doc:
The quotient `G ⧸ N` of a complete first countable uniform group `G` by a normal subgroup
is itself complete. In contrast to `QuotientGroup.completeSpace_left'`, in this version `G` is
already equipped with a uniform structure.
[N. Bourbaki, *General Topology*, IX.3.1 Proposition 4][bourbaki1966b]

Even though `G` is equipped with a uniform structure, the quotient `G ⧸ N` does not inherit a
uniform structure, so it is still provided manually via `IsTopologicalGroup.leftUniformSpace`.
In the most common use cases, this coincides (definitionally) with the uniform structure on the

`rankSums op tgt instructions` takes as input
* the name `op` of a binary operation,
* an `Expr`ession `tgt`,
* a list `instructions` of pair `(expression, Boolean)`.

It extracts the maximal subexpressions of `tgt` whose head symbol is `op`
(i.e. the maximal subexpressions that consist only of applications of the binary operation `op`),
it rearranges the operands of such subexpressions following the order implied by `instructions`
(as in `reorderUsing`),
it returns the list of pairs of expressions `(old_sum, new_sum)`, for which `old_sum ≠ new_sum`
sorted by decreasing value of `Lean.Expr.size`.
In particular, a subexpression of an `old_sum` can only appear *after* its over-expression.

signature.text:
def Mathlib.MoveAdd.rankSums (op : Lean.Name) (tgt : Lean.Expr)
  (instructions : List (Lean.Expr × Bool)) : Lean.MetaM (List (Lean.Expr × Lean.Expr))

value.text:
fun op tgt instructions => do
  let __do_lift ← Lean.instantiateMVars tgt
  let sums ← Mathlib.MoveAdd.getOps op __do_lift
  have candidates : Array (Option (Lean.Expr × Lean.Expr)) :=
    Array.map
      (fun x =>
        match x with
        | (addends, sum) =>
          have reord := Mathlib.MoveAdd.reorderUsing addends.toList instructions;
          have left_assoc? := sum.getAppFn.isConstOf `And || sum.getAppFn.isConstOf `Or;
          have resummed :=
            Mathlib.MoveAdd.sumList (Mathlib.MoveAdd.prepareOp sum) left_assoc? reord;
          if (resummed != sum) = true then some (sum, resummed) else none)
      sums
  pure
      (candidates.toList.reduceOption.toArray.qsort fun x y =>
          decide (y.1.sizeWithoutSharing ≤ x.1.sizeWithoutSharing)).toList

`move_oper op [a]` repeatedly moves `a` to the far right hand side in applications of `op`.
Here the constant `op` refers to a binary associative commutative operation, and `a` is any term
(potentially with underscores).

If `a` contains underscores, they are filled in by unification with the first matching occurrence.
Subterms with different values for the underscores are not matched, unless you repeat `a`.

Currently, `move_oper` supports the operators `HAdd.hAdd` (`· + ·`), `HMul.hMul` (`· * ·`),
`And` (`· ∧ ·`), `Or` (`· ∨ ·`), `Max.max` and `Min.min`. To support more operations, add them to
`Mathlib.MoveAdd.moveOperSimpCtx`.

* `move_add [...]` uses addition as the operation: it abbreviates `move_oper HAdd.add [...]`.
* `move_mul [...]` uses multiplication as the operation: it abbreviates `move_oper HMul.mul [...]`.
* `move_oper op [← a]` moves the atoms matching `a` to the far left hand side instead of the right.
* `move_oper op [a, b, ← c, ← d, ...]` moves multiple atoms simultaneously, in the order indicated
  by the arguments: `c` will appear to the left of `d` and `a` will appear to the left of `b`.

doc:
`reorderUsing toReorder instructions` produces a reordering of `toReorder : List α`,
following the requirements imposed by `instructions : List (α × Bool)`.

These are the requirements:
* elements of `toReorder` that appear with `true` in `instructions` appear at the
  *beginning* of the reordered list, in the order in which they appear in `instructions`;
* similarly, elements of `toReorder` that appear with `false` in `instructions` appear at the
  *end* of the reordered list, in the order in which they appear in `instructions`;
* finally, elements of `toReorder` that do not appear in `instructions` appear "in the middle"
  with the order that they had in `toReorder`.

For example,
* `reorderUsing [0, 1, 2] [(0, false)] = [1, 2, 0]`,
* `reorderUsing [0, 1, 2] [(1, true)] = [1, 0, 2]`,
* `reorderUsing [0, 1, 2] [(1, true), (0, false)] = [1, 2, 0]`.

signature.text:
def Mathlib.MoveAdd.reorderUsing.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [BEq α] (toReorder : List α)
  (instructions : List (α × Bool)) : List α

value.text:
fun {α} [BEq α] toReorder instructions =>
  have uInstructions :=
    match instructions.unzip with
    | (as, as?) => (Mathlib.MoveAdd.uniquify as).zip as?;
  have uToReorder := (Mathlib.MoveAdd.uniquify toReorder).toArray;
  have reorder :=
    uToReorder.qsort fun x y =>
      match List.find? (fun x_1 => x_1.1 == x) uInstructions,
        List.find? (fun x => x.1 == y) uInstructions with
      | none, none => decide ((uToReorder.idxOf? x).get! ≤ (uToReorder.idxOf? y).get!)
      | x_1, x_2 =>
        decide (Mathlib.MoveAdd.weight uInstructions x ≤ Mathlib.MoveAdd.weight uInstructions y);
  (Array.map Prod.fst reorder).toList

`permuteExpr op tgt instructions` takes the same input as `rankSums` and returns the
expression obtained from `tgt` by replacing all `old_sum`s by the corresponding `new_sum`.
If there were no required changes, then `permuteExpr` reports this in its second factor.

signature.text:
def Mathlib.MoveAdd.permuteExpr (op : Lean.Name) (tgt : Lean.Expr)
  (instructions : List (Lean.Expr × Bool)) : Lean.MetaM Lean.Expr

value.text:
fun op tgt instructions => do
  let permInstructions ← Mathlib.MoveAdd.rankSums op tgt instructions
  have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.MetaM Lean.Expr := fun __r =>
    have permTgt := tgt;
    do
    let __s ←
      forIn permInstructions permTgt fun x __s =>
          have permTgt := __s;
          match x with
          | (old, new) =>
            have permTgt :=
              Lean.Expr.replace (fun x => if (x == old) = true then some new else none) permTgt;
            pure (ForInStep.yield permTgt)
    have permTgt : Lean.Expr := __s
    pure permTgt
  if (permInstructions == []) = true then do
      let __r ← Lean.throwError (Lean.toMessageData "The goal is already in the required form")
      __do_jp __r
    else __do_jp ()

`unifyMovements` takes as input
* an array of `Expr × Bool × Syntax`, as in the output of `parseArrows`,
* the `Name` `op` of a binary operation,
* an `Expr`ession `tgt`.

It unifies each `Expr`ession appearing as a first factor of the array with the atoms
for the operation `op` in the expression `tgt`, returning
* the lists of pairs of a matched subexpression with the corresponding `Bool`ean;
* a pair of a list of error messages and the corresponding list of Syntax terms where the error
  should be thrown;
* an array of debugging messages.

signature.text:
def Mathlib.MoveAdd.unifyMovements (op : Lean.Name) (data : Array (Lean.Expr × Bool × Lean.Syntax))
  (tgt : Lean.Expr) :
  Lean.MetaM
    (List (Lean.Expr × Bool) × (List Lean.MessageData × List Lean.Syntax) × Array Lean.MessageData)

value.text:
fun op data tgt => do
  let ops ← Mathlib.MoveAdd.getOps op tgt
  have atoms : List Lean.Expr :=
    List.filter (fun x => !x.isBVar) (Array.map Prod.fst ops).flatten.toList
  let __x ← Mathlib.MoveAdd.pairUp data.toList atoms
  match __x with
    | (instr, neverMatched) =>
      have dbgMsg :=
        #[Lean.toMessageData "Matching of input variables:\n* pre-match:  " ++
                Lean.toMessageData (Array.map (Prod.snd ∘ Prod.snd) data) ++
              Lean.toMessageData "\n* post-match: " ++
            Lean.toMessageData instr,
          Lean.toMessageData "\nMaximum number of iterations: " ++ Lean.toMessageData ops.size];
      have errMsg :=
        List.map
          (fun x =>
            match x with
            | (t, a, stx) =>
              (if a = true then Lean.toMessageData "← " ++ Lean.toMessageData t
                else Lean.toMessageData t,
                stx))
          neverMatched;
      pure (instr, errMsg.unzip, dbgMsg)

`pairUp L R` takes two lists `L R : List Expr` as inputs.
It scans the elements of `L`, looking for a corresponding `DefEq` `Expr`ession in `R`.
If it finds one such element `d`, then it sets the element `d : R` aside, removing it from `R`, and
it continues with the matching on the remainder of `L` and on `R.erase d`.

At the end, it returns the sublist of `R` of the elements that were matched to some element of `L`,
in the order in which they appeared in `L`,
as well as the sublist of `L` of elements that were not matched, also in the order in which they
appeared in `L`.

Example:

doc:
`reorderAndSimp mv op instr` takes as input an `MVarId`  `mv`, the name `op` of a binary
operation and a list of "instructions" `instr` that it passes to `permuteExpr`.

* It creates a version `permuted_mv` of `mv` with subexpressions representing `op`-sums reordered
  following `instructions`.
* It produces 2 temporary goals by applying `Eq.mpr` and unifying the resulting meta-variable with
  `permuted_mv`: `[⊢ mv = permuted_mv, ⊢ permuted_mv]`.
* It tries to solve the goal `mv = permuted_mv` by a simple-minded `simp` call, using the
  `op`-analogues of `add_comm, add_assoc, add_left_comm`.

signature.text:
def Mathlib.MoveAdd.reorderAndSimp (op : Lean.Name) (mv : Lean.MVarId)
  (instr : List (Lean.Expr × Bool)) : Lean.MetaM (List Lean.MVarId)

value.text:
fun op mv instr =>
  mv.withContext do
    let __do_lift ← mv.getType''
    let permExpr ← Mathlib.MoveAdd.permuteExpr op __do_lift instr
    let __do_lift ← mv.getType
    let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.mkEq __do_lift permExpr
    let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.mkFreshExprMVar (some __do_lift)
    let eqmpr ← Lean.Meta.mkAppM `Eq.mpr #[__do_lift]
    let twoGoals ← mv.apply eqmpr
    guard ((twoGoals.length == 2) = true) <|>
        Lean.throwError
          (Lean.toMessageData "There should only be 2 goals, instead of " ++
            Lean.toMessageData twoGoals.length)
    let permGoal ←
      List.filterM
          (fun v => do
            let __do_lift ← v.isAssigned
            pure !__do_lift)
          twoGoals
    let __do_lift ← Mathlib.MoveAdd.moveOperSimpCtx
    let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.simpGoal permGoal[1]! __do_lift
    match __do_lift with
      | (some x, snd) =>
        Lean.throwError
          (Lean.toMessageData "'move_oper' could not solve " ++
            Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentD (Lean.MessageData.ofGoal x.2)))
      | (none, snd) => pure permGoal

doc:
Return a sorting key so that all `(a, true)`s are in the list's order
and sorted before all `(a, false)`s, which are also in the list's order.
Although `weight` does not require this, we use `weight` in the case where the list obtained
from `L` by only keeping the first component (i.e. `L.map Prod.fst`) has no duplicates.
The properties that we mention here assume that this is the case.

Thus, `weight L` is a function `α → ℤ` with the following properties:
* if `(a, true)  ∈ L`, then `weight L a` is strictly negative;
* if `(a, false) ∈ L`, then `weight L a` is strictly positive;
* if neither `(a, true)` nor `(a, false)` is in `L`, then `weight L a = 0`.

Moreover, the function `weight L` is strictly monotone increasing on both
`{a : α | (a, true) ∈ L}` and `{a : α | (a, false) ∈ L}`,
in the sense that if `a' = (a, true)` and `b' = (b, true)` are in `L`,
then `a'` appears before `b'` in `L` if and only if `weight L a < weight L b` and
similarly for the pairs with second coordinate equal to `false`.

signature.text: def Mathlib.MoveAdd.weight.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [BEq α] (L : List (α × Bool)) (a : α) : ℤ

value.text:
fun {α} [BEq α] L a =>
  have l := L.length;
  match List.find? (fun x => x.1 == a) L with
  | some (fst, b) => if b = true then -↑l + ↑(List.idxOf (a, b) L) else ↑(List.idxOf (a, b) L) + 1
  | none => 0

doc:
`prepareOp sum` takes an `Expr`ession as input.  It assumes that `sum` is a well-formed
term representing a repeated application of a binary operation and that the summands are the
last two arguments passed to the operation.
It returns the expression consisting of the operation with all its arguments already applied,
except for the last two.
This is similar to `Lean.Meta.mkAdd, Lean.Meta.mkMul`, except that the resulting operation is
primed to work with operands of the same type as the ones already appearing in `sum`.

This is useful to rearrange the operands.
